purpose: The endpoint and storage-prefix halves of G8.5, recorded the way docs/route-divergence.json records the route half. That file answers which routes exist, which verbs they export, which status their redirects emit and which buckets their migrations create. This one answers the two questions nothing asked: does every one of the register's 88 endpoint entries resolve to the contracts it names, and does every storage prefix the register declares describe the buckets and object keys the live code actually addresses. scripts/route-register-correspondence.test.ts compares every list below in both directions, so an unlisted divergence fails and a listed one that is fixed, moved or no longer reproducible fails too.
notAnApproval: Listing a divergence records it; it does not bless it. An endpoint whose success contract is undefined has no declared success status or body, and an object key no declared prefix describes has no declared filename contract, retention id or disposition. Each entry names what is missing and what closing it needs.
measured: 2026-09-10, against docs/route-register.json (160 routes: 62 pages, 88 endpoints, 10 redirects; 6 storagePrefixes over 4 buckets), src, worker/src, workers, supabase/migrations and docs/retention.md.

objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.why: The register declares three prefixes for the genomes bucket and every one of them partitions the bucket by account first: {account_id}/{subject_id}/{upload_id}/{filename}, {account_id}/{cohort_id}/{upload_id}/{filename}, and the legacy {user_id}/{uuid}/{name}. The live own-upload path uses none of them. private.issue_own_storage_upload_v1 sets staging_object_name to gen_random_uuid()::text and storage_bucket to 'genomes', and private finalization sets final_object_name to another bare gen_random_uuid(); both are single-segment keys at the root of the bucket. So the persistent object holding a person's genome sits at /<uuid>, and storage.subject-v2 describes a four-segment path that nothing writes. The filename half of the contract is honoured — the name is server-generated, opaque and single-segment, and no original filename reaches it — and the access half does not depend on the folder, because the upload RLS policy binds the exact server-generated key and the upload session's jti rather than a path prefix. What is not honoured is the declared shape itself, and with it the account and subject partition that the prefix, not the policy, is the record of.
objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.closing: Decide which document moves. Either the two prefixes are rewritten to the flat server-generated key the database actually issues — in which case the account and subject binding has to be stated as what it is, a database join rather than a path — or issuance and finalization are changed to build the declared path. The first is the smaller change and the more honest one; the second is what the register currently claims.
objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.blocker: authority — both halves are binding documents, and which one is wrong is an owner decision, not an implementation one.

objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.why: Prepared canonical artifacts are written into the same genomes bucket under a two-segment key whose first segment is the literal "prepared" — outside every declared prefix, and outside the account partition all three of them describe. preparedObjectKeySchema pins the shape and createPreparedArtifactWriter POSTs to /storage/v1/object/genomes/<that key>, so these are real objects holding derived genome data. The register knows the artifacts exist — policyContracts.own-prepared-object-v1 governs their lifecycle and preparation.scratch-2h their retention — and storagePrefixes, the file that says where bytes live and under what filename and retention contract, does not mention them. The same artifacts have a second home the register describes even less: the v2 receipt path writes them to Cloudflare R2 under a bucket matching ^inherit-prepared-[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$ (src/lib/genome/prepared-source/r2-transport.ts, served by workers/prepared-artifacts/worker.mjs through an env-bound R2 binding), and no storagePrefixes entry names any R2 bucket at all — the register's six prefixes cover four Supabase buckets and no second provider.
objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.closing: A storagePrefixes entry for prepared/{artifact_id} in genomes with its filename contract and the preparation.scratch-2h and publication retention ids, and a second entry — or a declared provider field on the first — for the R2 bucket family, so the two homes of the same artifact are both written down. The R2 half is the larger gap: a whole storage provider holding derived genome data is absent from the file that is supposed to enumerate them.
objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.blocker: none known — the lifecycle is decided and described in policyContracts; only the storage location is undeclared.

formRequestDivergenceNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5, form verification). What every <form> in the shipped app sends, read from source by scripts/form-contract-census.ts and held against docs/route-register.json by scripts/form-register-correspondence.test.ts: the target, method, body keys and literal discriminators, required and CSRF headers, Content-Type and the statuses the code branches on. A native form is read from its markup; an actionless form through its submit handler, following local and imported functions, conditional bodies and the props a form hands its submission to. Each row is one (request file, route, method) and the issues it shows, with the X-Inherit-CSRF omission kept in a row of its own that points at csrfTransportNote; the test computes the issue set and compares it with these rows in both directions, so a new divergence fails until recorded and a fixed one fails until its row is removed. closedBy names who has to act: owner (which document moves), counsel, or engineering. Listing a divergence records it; it does not bless it. 2026-10-23, owner decision ("G8.5: forms, CSRF, the server action and the Resend webhook", item 1): the register lists the harmless extras that ship, so five rows close and are removed: genome.browser's q (a closed queryContract), requestId on every subject-draft body, Path B's withAccount confirm body on api.withdraw, api.chat's 409s (copilot-provider-setup-required-v1 and own-chat-scientific-correction-v1) and api.future-person-claim's 404 (resource-not-found-v1). The CSRF rows are untouched: that work is item 2. The Path A row (src/components/family/invite-adult-form.tsx) closes the same day: the form and src/app/api/subject-drafts/route.ts moved to the registered { kind: "adult", adultFlow: "path-a-own-account", contactEmail, requestId, note? } and answer an unreviewed jurisdiction with capability-denied-api-v1 (403). The compatibility chat row (src/components/chat/chat-panel.tsx) closes the same day: the panel sends the registered { contextToken, message } to api.chat with no query, under a token /copilot/[scope] mints for the account, its auth session and the subject (src/lib/copilot/compat-chat-token.ts), and the route's AI SDK transport branch is gone.
csrfTransportNote: Every row whose issues are the X-Inherit-CSRF omission. The register makes X-Inherit-CSRF, a one-time token bound to the session, mandatory on every state-changing request of an authenticated or session-authenticated route (mutationSecurityBindings.csrfTransport; authContracts.authenticated-mutation-v1.csrf; token-api-v1.stateChangingRequest), and says an operation nonce is not CSRF (operationNonceIsNotCsrf). This form's request sends no such header. What the product relies on instead, read from the handlers rather than assumed: an exact Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin check, SameSite=Lax auth cookies and, where the register asks for one, a one-time operation nonce or form token in the body or the X-Inherit-Operation-Nonce header. So this is a real divergence between the register's CSRF transport and the defence the code implements, not a missing check on an open endpoint. Owner: decide which document moves. Either the register's csrfTransport stays and engineering builds the session-bound one-time X-Inherit-CSRF token (issue, bind, consume or rotate) on every listed route and its form, or the register is amended to name the Origin/Fetch-Metadata/SameSite-plus-nonce defence the code implements. Until then each row stays, and adding the header to a form without a handler that consumes it would make the row go stale without closing anything.

formRequestDivergence.why: Since 2026-10-23 (owner decision, G8.5 item 1) the form and src/lib/copilot/own-settings.ts use the register's three closed bodies, discriminated by mode (hosted, remote-openai-compatible, same-host-local) with camelCase apiKey and baseUrl, answer llm-settings-v1 ({ status: "saved", provider, endpointOrigin, classification } and { status: "deleted" }), and the DELETE consumes the X-Inherit-Operation-Nonce the page renders (remove_own_copilot_settings_with_nonce_v1, migration 20261024110000). Stored data is unchanged. One difference is left, on purpose: the register's hosted and remote-openai-compatible bodies say apiKey is required-bounded-secret, and the form sends apiKey only when one is typed, which the handler accepts. That keeps two behaviours the product has today and its tests rely on: re-saving the same destination keeps the stored key (the save door reuses it, and answers 409 key_required when the destination changed; llm-settings-form.test.ts "does not ask again for a stored key"), and a key-free HTTPS endpoint can be saved (every browser spec that saves the synthetic cloud endpoint, and the density fixture's fixed key-free cloud recipient). Making apiKey required would remove both, which is a product choice, not a transcription.
formRequestDivergence.closing: Owner: either the register's hosted and remote bodies say apiKey is optional (a stored key is kept for the same destination, and a key-free endpoint may be saved), and this row goes stale, or the key becomes required on every save, and engineering makes the form ask for it each time, drops the key-free path and changes the specs and the density fixture that save one. Until then the handler takes what the form sends.

formRequestDivergence.why: Sign-out is a native <form action="/auth/sign-out" method="post">, and the register's auth.sign-out requires X-Inherit-CSRF bound to the live session. A native submission can carry no custom header, and src/app/auth/sign-out/route.ts checks neither a header nor Origin before it calls signOut and clears the Tier-2 cookies, so its only cross-site defence is the SameSite=Lax attribute of the auth cookies; the browser suite also signs out with a bare page.request.post("/auth/sign-out"). The response is the 303 the register names, but src/app/auth/sign-out/response.ts sends it to / (and response.test.ts asserts that) where sign-out-v1 names auth.sign-in.
formRequestDivergence.closing: Owner: either the register keeps the header and sign-out becomes a script-submitted request carrying a session-bound token (engineering; changes sign-out without script and every browser spec that posts it bare), or the register names an Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site check, which engineering can add to the route without changing the form. Separately, which destination is right, / or /auth/sign-in.
